issues.failure_explanation: The text itself states that computing each entry y_{i_1...i_N} of Y requires exactly one division, and Y has n_1*...*n_N entries, so the total number of divisions is n_1*...*n_N. The paper instead asserts n_1*...*n_N*N divisions, overcounting by a factor N, and this wrong count is used as an input to the final operation-total formula.

failure_location.quote: Therefore, in order to fully determine $\Y$, we need $n_1n_2\ldots n_NN$ divisions

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the division count n_1*...*n_N*N by n_1*...*n_N (one division per entry, as the text's own per-entry count states) and adjust the final total accordingly (see ISSUE-002).
issues.overall_effect: The advertised exact flop count of the method (Section 2.1) is overstated by (N-1)*n_1*...*n_N divisions, and the final total inherits this error. The derived asymptotic statements (leading term about 5Nn^{N+1}, total cost O(n^{N+1})) are unaffected.
issues.title: Division count for computing Y overstated by a factor N
issues.why_classification: The repair is a local, forced recomputation of a single count; the method, the leading-order cost, the complexity class, and every advertised guarantee survive unchanged, and no labelled result depends on the exact count.

issues.failure_explanation: Writing P = n_1*...*n_N and S = sum_j n_j, the paper's own three summands evaluate to P/2*(5S-N) + P/2*(5S-3N-2) + PN = P(5S-N-1), but the display claims P(5S-N+1): the constant term has the wrong sign (-N-1 is correct, not -N+1), an error of 2P even taking the paper's own (itself erroneous, see ISSUE-001) division count as given; with the corrected division count P the true total is P(5S-2N).
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Recompute the sum: with the paper's division count the right-hand side is n_1*...*n_N[5 sum_j n_j - N - 1]; with the corrected division count of ISSUE-001 it is n_1*...*n_N[5 sum_j n_j - 2N].
issues.overall_effect: The paper's advertised exact floating-point-operation count (the abstract promises to 'calculate accurately the computational cost') is false as written; the equal-size consequence 'about 5Nn^{N+1}' and the O(n^{N+1}) complexity statement remain valid.
issues.title: Final operation-count equality evaluates incorrectly
issues.why_classification: Only a routine recomputation of the displayed sum is required; the correction changes solely lower-order terms while the leading term, the O(n^{N+1}) conclusion, and all downstream claims (timing trends, feasibility) are preserved, so every substantive claim survives.
